conventions.convention: S is finite, including S empty; V is the function space R^S with distinguished basis e_s. The Coxeter form has diagonal 1 and off-diagonal −cos(π/m), with cos(π/∞)=1. No definiteness or nondegeneracy is assumed. r_a is defined only when B(a,a)≠0.

The dual action is the left contragredient action (w·f)(v)=f(ρ(w)⁻¹v), even for degenerate B. C uses nonnegative simple-coordinate evaluations; C_I vanishes exactly on I and is strictly positive elsewhere.

The rank-two action on P* is through the matrix subgroup generated by r_s,r_t, not an asserted action of all W. In infinite dihedral type the chamber union is {f:f(e_s+e_t)>0}∪{0}; its nonzero boundary points are absent.
V is identified with V* through B only in finite type. Cosets are left cosets wW_I, I⊊S, ordered by reverse inclusion; C_I is open and its closure is the closed face.

Coset containment reverses geometric face containment: wW_I⊆vW_J iff v closure(C_J)⊆w closure(C_I). The realization map is radial normalization of the simplexwise affine map. At rank zero S⁻¹ is empty, and the complex has only the empty simplex and empty realization.

Basic-family existence and the general invariant-degree results assume AC. Basic degrees are sorted with multiplicity, d_i≥2, and e_i=d_i−1. Reducible degree multisets concatenate; rank-zero products are 1. The direct A2 and I2(m) computations require no AC.

B_C is the complex-bilinear extension, whereas the coefficient-factorial pairing is Hermitian and linear in its first argument. Δ uses the fixed positive unit roots. The Jacobian has invariant-equation rows and coordinate columns; its proportionality scalar depends on coordinates.

Spectral exponents are residues in {1,…,h−1}, counted with multiplicity. The additional D_n residue n−1, and hence degree n, is repeated when n is even. Recorded application order i_1,…,i_n gives matrix R_i_n⋯R_i_1; dual matrices are inverse transposes.

load_bearing.statement: For the finite-rank real Coxeter form, every r_a with B(a,a)≠0 is a B-preserving linear involution fixing the codimension-one kernel B(−,a). For distinct s,t, r_sr_t has exact order m(s,t) on V when m is finite, and infinite order when m=∞; in the latter case its restriction to P is I+N with N≠0 and N²=0.

The reflection assignment satisfies the Coxeter relators and gives a unique homomorphism ρ:W→GL(V). Every ρ(w) preserves B, every root has B-norm 1, and gr_ag⁻¹=r_ga for B-preserving g∈GL(V) and B(a,a)≠0; in particular ρ(wsw⁻¹)=r_ρ(w)e_s.

For a finite-type Coxeter system, U=V*, the arrangement complement is the disjoint union of the chambers wC° with closures wC, and every orbit meets C exactly once. Faces have the B-dual-basis cone descriptions. The map wW_I↦w closure(C_I) is bijective for I⊊S, reverses containment, and the intersection is w closure(C_(I∪J∪S(v⁻¹w))). For x∈wC_I, point and face setwise stabilizers are wW_Iw⁻¹. Radial normalization identifies the finite coset complex with S^(n−1), with the stated rank-zero convention.

If W is finite, there is a unique w₀ with w₀·C=−C, equivalently N(w₀)=Φ₊. It has length |Φ₊|=|T|, satisfies ℓ(w₀w)=ℓ(ww₀)=ℓ(w₀)−ℓ(w), squares to 1, and conjugates S to itself with ρ(w₀)e_s=−e_σ(s). Every finite W_I has the analogous unique longest element with ambient length equal to its intrinsic length.

The complexified canonical representation of any finite-type Coxeter system is faithful of dimension |S|, its image has order |W| and is generated by complex reflections, and its fixed vectors and invariant linear forms are zero. Under AC the stated polynomial-invariant, regular-sequence, freeness, Hilbert-series and order suppliers apply, including noncrystallographic and reducible types.

Under AC, minimal homogeneous basic families have the same degree multiset. Hilb(R,t)=∏(1−t^d_i)⁻¹, Hilb(A,t)=∏(1+t+⋯+t^(d_i−1)), dim A=∏d_i=|W|, and ∑(d_i−1) is the top degree. Molien’s identity uses the action on V_C* and the factor 1/|W|. Reducible degree multisets concatenate.

Under AC and n≥1, each coordinate x_j is algebraic over K=C(f₁,…,f_n), is not in K, and has minimal polynomial with nonzero derivative at x_j. There are rational coefficients b_ij satisfying δ_jk=∑_i b_ij ∂f_i/∂x_k. Consequently the invariant Jacobian is a nonzero polynomial.

Under AC, ∑(d_i−1)=N=|Φ₊|=|T|. In orthonormal real coordinates the invariant Jacobian is cΔ for c≠0, where Δ=∏_α∈Φ₊ B_C(−,α). The determinant anti-invariants are exactly ΔR, and [Δ] is nonzero and spans the one-dimensional top coinvariant component A_N with determinant action. Rank zero has Δ=J=1.

The contragredient formula defines a left linear action and every C_I is nonempty. The restricted finite rank-two matrix group has order 2m and tiles P* by 2m sectors simply transitively. In infinite rank two its chambers have disjoint interiors, union {δ>0}∪{0}, separating root walls, and integer wall traces on δ=1.

Under AC, for irreducible finite type the basic exponents equal the spectral residues of the bipartite Coxeter element, with multiplicity; their sum is |Φ₊|=nh/2, min d_i=2 and max d_i=h. The stated classical and exceptional degree tables follow. For reducible systems invariant algebras and coinvariant algebras tensor over components and degree multisets unite; rank zero and rank one are treated separately.

concerns.concern: The Statement introduction writes 'B(e_u,e_u)=B(e_z,e_z)=1, B(e_u,e_z)=−cos(π/m)' without defining e_u,e_z, immediately after defining u=x+iy and z=x−iy as complex coordinate functions. If these mean the coordinate vectors dual to u,z, their complex-bilinear self-pairings are zero, not one. Proof 1.1 correctly uses separate simple normals e₁,e₂. The Statement should make that basis distinction explicit.
